subject: Solstice Health - feature inclusion & short-term exception request
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Samir Gupta <samir@solsticehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 14 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Solstice Health - feature inclusion & short-term exception request

Marissa / Irene —

Quick context: Solstice is at contract signature and wants a mid-June go-live for an internal pilot. Their legal and procurement are signed off contingent on a short-lived operational concession: they need a per-tenant rate limiter override during the first 6 weeks of production to cover expected onboarding surges (3rd-party referral bursts).

As discussed with the buyer (Samir, cc'd), the minimal path to close is:
- A platform-level flag we can toggle per-tenant that temporarily relaxes the soft QPS limiter (no change to hard safety checks).
- A seeded cache / warmup pass for the primary model KV cache for the tenant before cutover.
- A routing rule to prefer a small reserved pool for Solstice for the first 30 days (billing as overage or pre-paid credit).

Can Product/Eng confirm: scope, estimated dev time, and risk profile (esp. telemetry and rollback plan)? If we can provide a written SOW Addendum and Ops playbook, Solstice will accept a short-term operational exception instead of a permanent product change.

Attachments: solstice-deal-econ.xlsx (deal economics), SOW_Solstice_v2.pdf (draft).

Ask: Can we get a go/no-go by EOD Friday 6/16? Sales needs this to finalize activation dates.

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter | Sr. Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Samir Gupta <samir@solsticehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 14 Jun 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Solstice Health - feature inclusion & short-term exception request

Ben — thanks for the heads up and the attachments. Looping in engineering for estimate (Irene).

A couple of clarifying questions before we commit to an approach:
- Is Solstice expecting this "override" to be exposed in the public API (i.e., programmatic flag) or can it be an org-level control in the Console managed by Redwood Ops?
- Do they require the bypass for all endpoints (generation/embeddings) or only for high-throughput generation paths?
- For the seeded cache, what TTL and volume are we talking about (approx token count / examples)?

Initial thought: if we can keep this as an Ops-managed, time-limited exception (Console toggle + routing rule) we can avoid a permanent product change. That still requires some engineering work for safe guardrails and auditing. If Ops can own the toggling and monitoring, Product can scope this as an "onramp exception" with a sunset clause in the SOW.

Irene — can you flag the minimal telemetry/events we need to make this safe? If the engineering cost is > 2 sprints, we should present the alternative (reserved pool + routing policy) to Solstice as a paid option.

Marissa
Marissa Cole | Group Product Manager, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Samir Gupta <samir@solsticehealth.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Jun 2028 08:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Solstice Health - feature inclusion & short-term exception request

Thanks — digging in from an engineering standpoint. Summary of options and estimated effort: 

Option A — Ops-managed toggle + short-lived bypass (preferred for speed):
- Implement a per-tenant Console toggle that relaxes the soft QPS limiter for specified routes. No change to hard safety checks.
- Add audit events and an automated rollback TTL (e.g., 30 days) enforced by the control plane.
- Seed tenant KV cache: scripting + one-time pre-warm job.
- Estimate: 2 engineering sprints (1 backend infra + 0.5 runtime + 0.5 ops tools). Risk: medium — must be careful around shared KV cache eviction and metric contamination.

Option B — Dedicated short-term pool + routing policy (lower product risk):
- Route Solstice traffic to a small dedicated pool for the 30-day period, no changes to limiter logic.
- Pre-seed the model cache on the dedicated pool.
- Estimate: 0.5 engineering sprint (orchestration + routing rule), Ops runbook for pool sizing. Risk: low — isolates blast radius. Cost: obvious customer cost (reserved capacity or overage credit).

Tradeoffs: Option A is faster but requires careful telemetry to avoid noisy neighbor issues. Option B is cleanest operationally and the smallest impact to platform code. Given the go-live timeline you mentioned, Option B looks more realistic unless Solstice will underwrite engineering time for Option A.

I've attached a brief proposal (routing-policy-proposal.md) that outlines the routing rule and rollback steps. If Sales can confirm budget for a 2-4 node reserved mini-pool for 30 days we can schedule the pool and the pre-warm window in Ops this week.

Irene
Irene Choi | Eng Lead, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
Attachment: routing-policy-proposal.md (stub)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Samir Gupta <samir@solsticehealth.com>, Nicole Park <nicole.park@solsticehealth.com>
Date: Sun, 17 Jun 2028 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Solstice Health - feature inclusion & short-term exception request

Appreciate the quick turn. Solstice Ops just confirmed budget for a 30-day reserved mini-pool (Samir, Nicole — thanks for the fast decision). They prefer the lower-risk path.

Next steps I propose:
1) Irene / Eng to trigger the routing rule and schedule the mini-pool provisioning window (target provisioning 6/20, pre-warm job 6/21).
2) Ops to run cache seeding script and validate metrics (Marissa / Laura to own the acceptance criteria).
3) Sales to finalize SOW addendum referencing the 30-day reserved pool and acceptance thresholds (Ben to send updated SOW).
4) Product to capture learnings and a boolean in the Console for future one-off pool routing (Marissa to log feature request, but this is not an immediate product ship).

Samir / Nicole — can you confirm the exact go-live cutoff (your internal pilot) and any additional acceptance checks besides latency and error-rate (e.g., throughput baseline)?

I'll circulate the SOW addendum shortly. Thanks all — good cross-functional move on timing.

Ben
Ben Carter | Sr. Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
Attachment referenced: SOW_Solstice_v2.pdf (updated SOW to follow)
